metadata.title: Resolution of the nominal 2025 database full-text nonretrieval set
metadata.scope: The 15 records advanced at title/abstract screening for which the initial retrieval pass did not identify an assessed full text.
metadata.decision_rule: A record was not excluded merely because retrieval failed. Clear or plausible qualitative-analysis contributions remain advance_core_not_retrieved until a reproducibly inspectable full text supports a final eligibility decision. Master-ready evidence and quality rows were made only for inspected full texts.

summary.arithmetic_check: 15 = 10 recovered/assessed + 5 not retrieved; 10 recovered/assessed = 8 core + 1 adjacent + 1 excluded.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence to Support Qualitative Data Analysis: Promises, Approaches, Pitfalls.
records.record_specific_reason: The inspected article directly tests an LLM on qualitative-data-analysis tasks and reports both successful summarization/counting and substantive failures in coding, thematic synthesis, evidence quotation, and rerun stability.

records.title: Automating Thematic analysis of COVID-19 Vaccine Hesitancy in Alaska with multi-agent LLM systems
records.record_specific_reason: The abstract describes multi-agent LLM thematic analysis of 87 semi-structured interviews, with agents representing four disciplinary perspectives and producing five themes. This is plausibly core, but the TechRxiv DOI and manuscript endpoint did not yield a reproducibly inspectable full text, so no methodological or performance claims beyond the abstract were extracted.

records.title: Can Large Language Models Perform Inductive Qualitative Coding? - Evaluating GPT-4 on Korean-Language Texts
records.record_specific_reason: The official metadata abstract reports GPT-4 inductive coding of 497 Korean documentary quotations, including BERTScore and character-level agreement results. This is plausibly core and uniquely informative for non-English evaluation, but the journal/KISS full text was access-restricted; abstract-only results were not promoted to a 52-field extraction or quality score.
retrieval_attempts: Official journal/KCI/KISS record and full-text endpoints

records.title: Data Plus Theory Equals Codebook: Leveraging LLMs for Human-AI Codebook Development
records.record_specific_reason: The inspected manuscript evaluates data-only, theory-only, and data-plus-theory prompting for collaborative codebook generation and reports theory alignment and practical-applicability ratings.

records.title: Emergent Convergence in Multi-Agent LLM Annotation
records.record_specific_reason: The inspected BlackboxNLP paper studies 7,500 multi-agent discussions on an inductive coding task and directly demonstrates that interactional convergence can flatten semantic distinctions without establishing coding quality.

records.title: Evaluating LLM Assisted Qualitative Analysis in Medical Education Research: A Comparison of Human and AI-Generated Thematic Coding (Preprint)
records.record_specific_reason: The official preprint abstract reports GPT-4o coding of a four-participant medical-student focus group and separate inductive and deductive comparisons, including code-level agreement and kappa. It is plausibly core, but the official preprint manuscript was not reproducibly retrievable; no abstract-only extraction or quality score was created.
retrieval_attempts: Official JMIR Preprints record and manuscript endpoints

records.title: Exploring Inductive and Deductive Qualitative Coding with AI: Investigating Inter-Rater Reliability between Large Language Model and Human Coders
records.record_specific_reason: The inspected proceedings paper directly compares LLM and human coding under inductive and deductive conditions and reports model-human and model-self reliability, making it eligible despite important design limitations.

records.title: Human–AI Collaboration Pipeline for Thematic Analysis: Example of VR-Supported Pulmonary Rehabilitation
records.record_specific_reason: Official metadata describes a three-agent thematic-analysis pipeline applied to interviews from nine VR pulmonary-rehabilitation participants and reports a Sentence-T5-XXL similarity comparison. This is plausibly core, but the exact 2025 IEEE full text was not reproducibly available. A related 2026 report was not treated as proof that this conference paper had been inspected.
records.version_family_alert: A related expanded 2026 article exists, but exact study/version equivalence was not established for this resolution.

records.title: Integrating Qualitative Comparative Analysis With Reflexive Thematic Analysis in Theme Development
records.record_specific_reason: Full-text inspection establishes that 'QCA' means qualitative comparative analysis and that the article integrates that human analytic method with reflexive thematic analysis. It contains no AI, LLM, computational analyst, or directly applicable computational-evaluation contribution.

records.title: Large Language Model Versus Human-Generated Thematic Analysis in Otolaryngology Qualitative Research.
records.record_specific_reason: The title and indexed metadata explicitly describe a human-versus-LLM thematic-analysis comparison, so the paper remains plausibly core. The short Laryngoscope article was not available through a reproducibly inspectable publisher, repository, or indexed full-text endpoint; no methodological claims were inferred from its title.

records.title: Narrative-Integrated Thematic Analysis (NITA): AI-Supported Theme Generation Without Coding
records.record_specific_reason: The current peer-reviewed 2026 version was inspected. It presents and applies a human-led narrative-integrated, noncoding/abductive workflow for AI-supported theme generation and is extracted once for the publication family.
records.version_family_alert: The screened 2025 SSRN record and 2026 NITA version are one publication family; count once.

records.title: Qualitative Research in the Age of LLMs: A Human-in-the-Loop Approach to Hybrid Thematic Analysis
records.record_specific_reason: The inspected ICLS paper presents a source-linked human-in-the-loop thematic workflow and reports an empirical application; its retained status is tempered by methodological incongruence between reflexive-TA language and codebook/reliability operations.

records.title: The application of large language models in qualitative nursing research: A scoping review.
records.record_specific_reason: The inspected scoping review synthesizes 11 nursing studies of LLM-supported qualitative research. It informs reporting and evidence-gap claims but is adjacent rather than a primary system evaluation, and its included studies must not be double-counted as independent evidence.

records.title: Updating “The Future of Coding”: Qualitative Coding with Generative Large Language Models
records.record_specific_reason: The inspected Sociological Methods & Research article evaluates zero-shot, chain-of-thought, and few-shot LLM coding against established human-coded article corpora with class-sensitive F1 and reliability analyses.
records.dependency_alert: Uses prior McCall (2013) and Nelson (2018) corpora/codings; do not treat reused human labels as a new independent qualitative dataset.

records.title: Using Generative AI for Qualitative Coding
records.record_specific_reason: The inspected Library Trends paper replicates a prior human qualitative analysis with ChatGPT-4 and directly documents differences in code volume, thematic content, contextual sensitivity, and analyst time.
records.dependency_alert: Reuses the Surbaugh et al. (2024) interview corpus and human analysis; count as one computational comparison but not as a new independent data collection.
